model_output_raw.confidence_explanation: The evidence shows a clear pattern of an authorized user (user_04) with 'read_only' access and a baseline of 0 downloads per day performing 6 file downloads. Crucially, this user accessed files outside their department (Engineering projects) and worked significantly outside their normal hours (until 19:00). This behavior deviates sharply from the user's baseline and role, indicating unauthorized data exfiltration consistent with an insider threat.

attack_chain.description: user_04 logs in from normal IP within normal hours.
user_04 performs first download (accounts_receivable), violating baseline of 0 downloads/day.
user_04 performs second download (accounts_payable), establishing a pattern of bulk data collection.
user_04 accesses Engineering project data (project_alpha), crossing departmental boundaries.
user_04 downloads sensitive tax data, continuing exfiltration pattern.
user_04 accesses second Engineering project (project_beta), expanding scope of unauthorized access.
user_04 downloads bank reconciliation data, high-value financial asset.
user_04 downloads general ledger, a comprehensive financial record.
user_04 accesses Engineering deliverables outside normal hours (17:15), indicating evasion of standard monitoring.
user_04 logs out at 19:00, well past normal hours (17:00), completing the session.

gaps: No metadata (ticket numbers or justification) provided for the cross-department access or off-hours activity.
No network egress logs to confirm if the downloaded files were successfully transferred outside the private cloud.
No information on whether user_04 has a legitimate business reason (e.g., audit, cross-functional project) for accessing Engineering data.
model_output_raw.narrative: user_04, a junior accountant with read-only access and a baseline of zero daily downloads, engaged in a systematic exfiltration of financial and engineering data. The user downloaded six files, including sensitive ledgers and tax records, and accessed engineering project directories outside their department and normal working hours. This pattern of behavior strongly indicates an insider threat attempting to steal proprietary data.
